headline_findings: The printed text is mostly frame: in the 33 printed producer heads (563,438 characters) the instruction frame (callback, recovery, goal and Checked by, Until Loop block, status, rules, chrome) is 39.2%, the stage method 26.7%, step and stage input 15.0%, quoted state only 3.0%.

By-value state is what the head drops first: 23 of 28 packets with quoted hand-offs printed none of them, 15 of 33 printed no References block (so RUN/HOME/GUIDES were undefined in the printed text), and every inner head cut W1's 3,308-character work item context to a 400-character excerpt.

10 of 33 prints passed Grok's 20,000-character cut and lost their middle (7 of 8 implement prints, the revisit step-plan, verify, carry-forward): implement lost parts of duty items 5-7 and Code craft rules 1-2, the revisit step-plan lost the middle of duty 4's `check` rule. The head table's fixture (node-fix-bug) predicts implement at 16,104; real step data put it at 19.5-24.8 KB.

Consequence in the run: step-plan read spec.md, architecture.md and environment.md whole (48.7 KB) and ShipLoop's own scripts 29 times, and reached the plan and prepare results through RUN/inbox copies while the list naming them was not printed; implement S1 read architecture.md whole although its packet file quoted every AD-<n> by value.

5,790 characters of every packet file are lines identical in all 33 packets (paths included); absolute paths alone are 9.3% of printed text. Each rule about check-only, recovery, pause and 'untrusted' input is stated 2-5 times per packet; step-plan states each structural rule three times (duty, exit condition, Checked by).

25% of the planning duty text (12,340 of 48,737 characters across intake..test-spec) did not apply to the Battleship run (empty checkout, single-user stateless app): service, MCP, connected-knowledge, current-system, bootstrap, module-format and optional Backchain-child items.
Ten duty items rewritten: 12,849 -> 6,874 characters (-46%) while adding the accepted plan units B1, B2, C1, A1, A4, G4, G6, H4.

Strict templates (owner direction) are feasible and testable: the prototype renders step-plan and implement for Battleship S1 at 19,643 and 18,794 printed characters with the work item context, concern rows, ## Commands, the step's R-<n> and AD-<n> by value, where today's heads carried none of them.

The template validator turns the 20,000-character budget into a build-time check: with today's producer data it refuses both templates (worst cases 21,204 and 20,660); with producer-side bounds (context 2,500, step task 700, Proof 600, criteria 1,200) implement passes at 18,760 and step-plan misses by 84.

Recommendation: yes, migrate to one template per stage plus shared partials, with bounds enforced at the producing stage's gate, elastic input pools, gate IDs, and a byte-identical pilot of step-plan and implement first.

- `check`: the one command, from the repository root, that proves the step's criteria with only this step and
     accepted earlier ones; ShipLoop runs it at the step's done. It needs no later step, unwritten test or release
     artifact (reuse a recorded command that proves them); skipping a missing file, or asserting only that a file
     exists where behaviour is asked, proves nothing. Remote-only target: the recorded test route only. None runs
     now: change the step boundary.
rewrites.after: - `check`: the one command, from the repository root, that proves the step's criteria with only this step and accepted earlier ones; ShipLoop runs it at the step's done. It observes behaviour: matching the implementation's own text (a literal, a call shape) dictates form and proves nothing, and so does skipping a missing file. It needs no later step, unwritten test or release artifact. Behaviour that runs only on a remote target: deploy only this step's paths to the recorded development target, then run a read-only probe the run's authority covers.
